title: Client stub patterns and smoke-lab brainstorm
content:
Context
This is a lightweight working doc to capture an idea for a small, opinionated client stub pattern + smoke-lab that helps new integrators (internal and early pilot customers) get a reproducible, observable first call experience in ~10 minutes. Goal: reduce first-call friction, capture minimal telemetry, and exercise common failure modes so the DX (developer experience) team and SDK engineers can triage quickly.

Scope / constraints
- Focused on Redwood hosted API and local dev-runner (sdk stub) flow.
- Minimal dependencies: node/python examples only. No heavy infra required.
- Surface design/contract guidance for client stub, quick smoke test, and telemetry events to ship in SDK v0.8 quickstart.
- Keep onboarding flow < 10 steps, can be followed in a terminal or quick web UI.

Principles
- Opinionated defaults: provide a single recommended path that "just works" for typical devs.
- Fast feedback: if something fails, error messages point to a remediation step (e.g., auth, network, quota).
- Observable and actionable telemetry: capture a few fields that help debug without exposing PII.
- Reproducible: deterministic sample prompts and response asserts in the smoke script.

Quickstart user journey (10-min path)
1) sign up / grab API key (assume user already has one for quickstart)
2) clone repo: git clone github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-stubs && cd sdk-stubs/quickstart
3) install: npm install OR pip install -r requirements.txt
4) set env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-...
5) run smoke: npm run smoke OR python smoke.py
6) expect: sample chat response printed + small JSON telemetry summary (locally)
7) if fails: script prints one-line diagnosis and link to troubleshooting snippet in README

Client stub design (opinionated)
- Purpose: a tiny multi-language wrapper that simulates network, auth, and the minimal behavior of Redwood's hosted API for local dev. Not a full emulator of runtime performance.
- Size target: single-file entry (<= 120 lines JS / PY) + README.
- Behavior: accepts the same request shape as the SDK (messages, model, max_tokens), returns a canned response or proxies to real API when REDWOOD_API_KEY present.
- Modes:
  - offline (default): deterministic canned responses for prompts listed in fixtures/
  - online: forwards to Redwood API, but captures full telemetry in local log and emits a short diagnostics summary
- Error simulation flags: --simulate-latency-ms, --simulate-rate-limit, --simulate-kvcache-miss to reproduce common customer issues.

Sample stub pseudo-interface (JS)
// usage: node stub.js --mode offline
async function send(request) {
  // validate shape, basic TTL check
  if (request.messages[0].content.includes('greet')) {
    return { id: 'stub-1', choices: [{ text: 'Hello from stub!' }], usage: { tokens: 12 } }
  }
  return { id: 'stub-2', choices: [{ text: 'Default stub reply' }], usage: { tokens: 8 } }
}

Smoke-lab tests (high level)
- test-smoke: run a single happy-path generation, assert response contains expected token fragment.
- test-streaming: exercise streaming API (JS only) and assert chunk ordering.
- test-auth-missing: run with no key and assert script errors with actionable message.
- test-rate-limit: run stub with --simulate-rate-limit and assert client retries/backoff path exercised.
- test-telemetry-format: runs quick local check that telemetry JSON includes required keys.

Telemetry / diagnostic payload (local minimal set)
- event: smoke_start | smoke_end | smoke_fail
- client_version: e.g., js-0.8.0
- mode: offline | online
- test_name: test-smoke
- outcome: pass | fail
- duration_ms: numeric
- error_code: short string (if fail)
- sample_prompt_hash: sha1(prefix) // non-reversible id to correlate prompt set
- env: REDWOOD_REGION (optional)
Notes: do not send user prompt text to central telemetry in pilot. Locally saved telemetry should remain on disk by default and optionally upload via explicit --upload flag for customers who opt-in.

README / onboarding copy (short)
- what this is: a tiny local stub + smoke tests to make sure your app can make a first call and recover from common failures.
- step-by-step: the 7 steps from Quickstart user journey.
- when to use offline vs online: offline = fast iteration, online = integration + perf check.
- privacy note: no production keys are stored. sample prompts are fixtures.

Developer checklist for shipping in SDK repo
- [ ] implement stub for JS and Python parity (same flags and env vars)
- [ ] add smoke scripts to CI as a quick pipeline step (non-blocking flaky-exempt)
- [ ] include telemetry local logger and optional uploader behind --upload flag
- [ ] README + 3-line quickstart in top-level README.md
- [ ] add a short troubleshooting section with 6 common errors and exact remediation commands
- [ ] add unit tests for flag parsing and error messages

Edge cases and unresolved questions
- Should stub include a minimal token/usage calculator to exercise cost UI? (Pros: exercise usage path. Cons: misleading for customers.)
- How much of KV cache behavior should be simulated? A small cache hit/miss toggle seems useful but avoid complexity.
- Ownership: eng-developer-experience owns README and smoke content; eng-serving-runtime should review behavioral fidelity for online forwarding.
- Metrics export policy: confirm privacy/legal stance on sending any hashed prompt ids to central telemetry. Need sign-off from security-and-compliance.

Acceptance criteria for pilot (internal)
- New hire (non-SWE, e.g., Solutions Engineer) can complete quickstart in < 10 minutes and get a passing smoke result.
- Two pilot customers run quickstart and report whether the troubleshooting hints were sufficient.
- CI runs smoke-lab on PRs for SDK changes and flags obvious breaking changes (simple detection).

Next steps (short-term)
1) small spike: build JS stub + smoke scripts (2 engineer-days)
2) verify telemetry fields and privacy constraints with Security (1/2 day)
3) build Python parity stub + README (1.5 engineer-days)
4) run internal pilot with 3 non-dev team members (1 day)
5) iterate wording in onboarding and land in SDK repo as docs + smoke folder

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- Keep canned responses diverse but short (<= 60 tokens) so smoke passes without heavy runtime.
- Add quick link in console docs: "Run quick smoke" that opens a modal with the 7 steps.
- Consider adding a tiny web UI that calls stub on localhost for non-terminal folks (low priority).

Links & references
- previous: https://confluence.redwood.dev/display/DEVX/first-call-experience (draft)
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-stubs/pull/142 (proto)
- legal/privacy: security-and-compliance/smoke-telemetry-guidelines.md

This doc is intentionally terse. Use this as the seed for an actionable PR in the SDK repo (folder: quickstart/smoke).
